clue.text: Score in Scrabble for "POET"?

parts.note: the points a played word earns in Scrabble are what that word is worth; split the same way, the phrase names the Lake District poet William

explanation.surface: A puzzled player wonders how many points the word POET would score on a Scrabble board.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as WORD'S WORTH, the value of a word in Scrabble; run together it is the Romantic poet William Wordsworth, the poet of the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: William Wordsworth was a leading English Romantic poet, and the phrase also states a word's points value in the game.

clue.text: Expects a couple to be lacking sound judgement

indicators.note: lacking something means it is missing, so these letters are taken away

parts.note: to await is to expect
a couple of the letter A, i.e. two of them

explanation.surface: Someone predicts a pair will show poor sense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a couple' is two As, both removed from AWAITS.
explanation.definitionFit: Good sense and mental sharpness, as in keeping one's head, is a common plural sense.

clue.text: Openly sexual and flash to eat meal topless

indicators.note: eating puts food inside, so the trimmed meal goes inside the flash word

parts.note: a ray is a flash or beam of light

indicators.note: without its top, the word loses its first letter

parts.note: lunch is a midday meal

explanation.surface: Racy and showy, eating a meal without a top on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'topless' removes the first letter of the meal, and 'to eat' puts what is left inside the flash.
explanation.definitionFit: Crude, earthy and frankly sexual is the usual sense of this slangy adjective.

clue.text: Cruise perhaps to Italian capital with single cost being flexible

indicators.note: letters that are flexible can bend into a new order
a capital is a first, upper-case letter

explanation.surface: A holiday cruise to Rome, with one adaptable price.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cruise' is Tom Cruise, not a holiday; 'being flexible' rearranges TO, I and SINGLE COST.
explanation.definitionFit: The actor Tom Cruise is a prominent member of the Church founded by L. Ron Hubbard, an example of a follower.

clue.text: Expense of transposing each half of design

indicators.note: the two halves of the word swap places

parts.note: a layout is a design or plan

explanation.surface: The cost involved in swapping both halves of a plan.
explanation.walkthrough: LAY-OUT with its halves swapped gives OUT-LAY.
explanation.definitionFit: Money laid out or spent on something is an expenditure.

clue.text: Disguise attempt to pinch an undergarment

indicators.note: to pinch is to grip, so the letters are held within the attempt word

parts.note: a try is an attempt
a vest is an undergarment, in Britain worn under a shirt

explanation.surface: A masquerade: someone tries to steal underwear.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a vest is a sleeveless undershirt.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally a dressing up in another's clothes, the word means a grotesque imitation or disguise.

clue.text: It's frequently hailed a classic US sitcom

definitions.meaning: a cab is the thing people wave down in the street
the American comedy series about New York cab drivers, 1978-83

explanation.surface: Something praised again and again, an old American comedy show.
explanation.definitionFit: A cab is hailed from the kerb, and the long-running American comedy about cabbies bore the same name.

clue.text: Element extracted from heart of Alaska

definitions.text: Element extracted from heart of Alaska

parts.words: Element extracted from heart of Alaska
parts.note: the heart of Alaska is its middle two letters, A and S, which form the chemical symbol of the element

explanation.surface: A mineral mined in the middle of Alaska.
explanation.walkthrough: The middle letters of AL-AS-KA are AS, the symbol of the poisonous element; the clue gives the symbol, not the name's letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This poisonous semi-metal, atomic number 33, has the chemical symbol As.

clue.text: Weak-willed Tories' rule in tatters

indicators.note: torn to shreds, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Conservative government falling apart is feeble.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking firmness of purpose and unable to decide means being indecisive.

clue.text: Trains regularly caught by solicitor, one who's sightseeing

indicators.note: something caught by another is held inside it, so the picked letters sit within the solicitor word

parts.note: a tout is someone who solicits custom, e.g. for tickets

indicators.note: taking letters at regular intervals: here the second, fourth and sixth of the word trains

explanation.surface: Railway services are regularly taken by a lawyer, a traveller out seeing the sights.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solicitor' looks like a lawyer but is a tout, one who solicits trade; 'regularly' picks RIS from Trains.
explanation.definitionFit: A visitor taking in the sights of a place is a holidaymaker of this kind.

clue.text: Teacher varied changes to keep close to syllabus

indicators.note: one part keeps another inside it, so the final letter goes within the rearranged letters
the word varied is changed, its letters rearranged
the close of a word is its end, so its last letter

explanation.surface: An instructor made assorted alterations in order to stay near the course outline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changes' rearranges VARIED into ADVIER, and 'to keep' puts S, the close of syllabus, inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutor or counsellor who guides a student is a mentor of this kind, giving guidance and instruction.

clue.text: Papers consumed by immorality existing in position Humphrey once occupied

parts.note: vice is immorality

indicators.note: being consumed puts one thing inside another, so the papers go into the existing word

parts.note: present means existing now
ID is identification papers

explanation.surface: Newspapers swallowed up by depravity, a scandal at the heart of politics.
explanation.walkthrough: Hubert Humphrey was US vice president under Lyndon Johnson, 1965-69.
explanation.definitionFit: Hubert Humphrey served as Lyndon Johnson's deputy, the second-highest office in the US government.

clue.text: Beers conceived originally in monasteries — they're gradually gaining in strength

indicators.note: one group of letters goes in another, so the beer word and the letter go inside the religious houses

parts.note: convents are religious houses, monasteries for nuns
ales are beers

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its beginning, so its first letter

explanation.surface: Ales first brewed by monks, a picture of monastery brewing.
explanation.walkthrough: ALES and C (conceived originally) go 'in' CONVENTS: CONV-ALES-C-ENTS.
explanation.definitionFit: People recovering from illness slowly regain their health and strength, which is what the definition describes.

clue.text: South Korean typically advertises engine parts

parts.note: Park is one of the commonest Korean surnames
to plug something is to promote it

explanation.surface: A South Korean firm promotes its motor components.
explanation.definitionFit: These devices fire the fuel mixture in a petrol engine's cylinders, so they are components.

clue.text: Suffer the consequences of having no school ultimately to represent

indicators.note: having none of something means it is taken away from the phrase

parts.note: to play for a team or country is to represent it

indicators.note: ultimately means at the end, so the final letter

explanation.surface: Someone is punished because their school has nobody to stand for it.
explanation.walkthrough: PLAY FOR (represent, as a sportsman does) loses L, the last letter of school.
explanation.definitionFit: To suffer the results of a misdeed is idiomatically to be made to settle the bill for it.

clue.text: City pal possibly pursues American's tip? That's unusual

indicators.note: the rearranged letters follow, or chase, the single letter
the tip of a word is its first letter
possibly signals the letters of city pal could be arranged another way

explanation.surface: A friend from the city chases an American for a gratuity, which is out of the ordinary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges CITY PAL into TYPICAL, which 'pursues' A, the tip of American's.
explanation.definitionFit: Something out of the ordinary is not representative of its type.

clue.text: Count upon actor briefly to stop working

indicators.note: made brief, the name is cut short by its last letter

parts.note: Johnny Depp is the American actor
to end is to stop
on means working, as a switched-on machine is

explanation.surface: Rely on a performer to give up his job soon.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to trust them to come through, the same sense as counting on.

clue.text: Content to stare as One Direction argued

indicators.note: the content of a phrase is what is held within it, so the letters are found inside these words

explanation.surface: Happy to gaze as the boy band One Direction quarrelled among themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Content' looks like 'happy' but means what is contained: the answer lies in staRE AS ONE Direction.
explanation.definitionFit: To argue a case is to put it logically, setting out a line of thought.

clue.text: Shied away from poster describing video nasty

indicators.note: to describe a circle is to draw round, so the poster word goes around the rest

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement such as a poster

indicators.note: nasty signals the letters are messed up

explanation.surface: Steered clear of a billboard showing a horror film.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'video nasty' was the 1980s British name for a violent horror film on video; the phrase is split, with 'nasty' as the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To steer clear of or dodge something is to keep away from it.

clue.text: Allow hotel to open for quiet, solitary individual

indicators.note: the hotel letter takes the opening place in place of the quiet letter

parts.note: to allow is to permit
P (piano) is the musical marking for quiet
H is hotel in the phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Letting a hotel open for a quiet, solitary guest.
explanation.walkthrough: In PERMIT the initial P (quiet) is replaced by H (hotel), which 'opens' the word.
explanation.definitionFit: A recluse who lives apart from society is the classic solitary person.

clue.text: Screen giving warning is inadequate

indicators.note: falling short, the word lacks its final letter

parts.note: monitory is an adjective meaning giving a warning or admonition

explanation.surface: A cinema or TV screen showing a warning is not good enough.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is inadequate' drops the last letter, Y, from MONITORY.
explanation.definitionFit: A display such as a computer's is a visual unit of this kind.

clue.text: Misinterpret clothing left loose at the back

parts.note: garb is clothing

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so its last letter

explanation.surface: Getting the wrong idea from clothes that hang loose behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To muddle or distort a message is to confuse its meaning.

clue.text: Quota opposed to abortion initially shows increase

indicators.note: the anti-abortion stance comes initially, ahead of the share

parts.note: pro-life describes those campaigning against abortion
a ration is a fixed allowance or quota

explanation.surface: Allocations set by anti-abortion campaigners show signs of growth.
explanation.definitionFit: Rapid multiplication or spread in numbers is a growth of exactly this kind.

clue.text: Predicament whether one chooses jam or pickle

explanation.surface: Whether you pick jam or pickle, you are in a difficult spot.
explanation.walkthrough: A triple definition: all three of predicament, jam and pickle mean the same plight.
explanation.definitionFit: A fix or muddle is a plight, and both jam and pickle are slang for one.

clue.text: Given the latest news, excited romantic partner anticipates diamonds

indicators.note: to anticipate is to come before, so the partner word precedes the suit letter

parts.note: up can mean excited or stirred, as in 'het up'
a date is someone one is courting
D is the abbreviation for diamonds in card games

explanation.surface: An eager lover expects jewellery after hearing the latest gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone briefed on recent developments has been brought up to speed with current information.

clue.text: Inspire brother to face weather unprotected

indicators.note: with its protective outer layer removed, the word loses its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Encourage a sibling to brave the storm without a coat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unprotected' strips the outer letters from weather to leave EATHE.
explanation.definitionFit: To inspire in its literal sense is to draw air into the lungs, i.e. to inhale.

clue.text: Fusses about something to add to drink

indicators.note: about means turned round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: ados are fusses, as in 'much ado'

explanation.surface: Making a fuss over what should go in a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Fizzy water is a mixer poured into a spirit such as whisky.

clue.text: Risks advocate coming out in favour of Indian contracts

indicators.note: one abbreviation comes out of the word and another takes its place

parts.note: adventures are risky undertakings
ADV is the standard abbreviation for advocate
IND is the abbreviation for Indian

explanation.surface: A lawyer speaks out for Indian agreements despite the dangers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coming out in favour of' replaces ADV in ADVENTURES with IND; 'in favour of' looks like support but means 'replaced by'.
explanation.definitionFit: These are formal agreements binding an apprentice or servant to work for a master for a set term.
